about: Registry of every figure, diagram, table, screenshot and audio example the Arp manual page (docs/manual/arp.md) needs, in horde's docs/manual/figures.json shape so horde can merge the entries when it copies the page in (chapter = arp). One entry per [[FIG:id]] / [[TAB:id]] / [[AUD:id]] placeholder in the page; tools/gen_manual_params.py --check keeps the two in step. The settings reference is NOT a placeholder: it is generated into the page between its markers. Field meanings and statuses: horde docs/manual/README.md.

entries.purpose: Show the reader where the Arp controls are.
entries.content: The Arp page of horde's interface with the module on, a chord held and the default settings; the on switches, Order, Pattern, Rate, Latch and the chord stage visible.
entries.source: GUI 3 Arp page, once built (the panel path is marked *(page pending)* in the text)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear the default arpeggio before changing anything.
entries.content: About 16 beats: a held C, E, G, B played Up in even sixteenths at the default settings.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 01-baseline (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Show what each of the 16 order styles plays over the same held notes.
entries.content: One row per Order choice (by its display name): the note sequence one full cycle plays over four held notes C, E, G, B (a chord or dyad shown as bracketed notes), and the cycle length for one, two and four held notes.
entries.source: spec/SPEC.md §4.2 order table; check the sequences against the order tour (tests/core/render.cpp scenarios 02a-order-tour-1 and 02b-order-tour-2) or the lab's pattern view

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear all 16 order styles over one chord.
entries.content: Two files of eight bars each: the same four held notes in all 16 orders, one bar per order, labelled.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 02a-order-tour-1 and 02b-order-tour-2 (two files, one entry) (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear the 11 bank patterns.
entries.content: Two files: one bar per pattern over a rising arpeggio, from Plain to Trigger pulse (the trigger clicks are the renderer's stand-in for a signal event).
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 03a-pattern-tour-1 and 03b-pattern-tour-2 (two files, one entry) (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Show what one pattern step carries.
entries.content: One step drawn as a card with its fields and ranges: play, tie, velocity 0-200 %, gate 1-200 %, step -8..+8, chance 0-100 %, ratchet 1-4, trigger 0-8, pick (order, 1-8, low, high, chord); the pattern-level step size and unit beside it.

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear a roll, a tie and a chance step.
entries.content: Three patterns over the baseline: Roll at the end, Tied legato at the default gate, Sparse chance (the same on every render).
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 13-ratchets-ties-chance (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Show how to build and save a pattern of your own.
entries.content: The step editor with a 16-step pattern open: each step's fields, the pattern's step size and unit, and the library of saved patterns.
entries.source: Not designed: where the editor lives in horde and how presets carry the user pattern are with horde (Q-H6); the lab's build-your-own editor (lab/arp-lab.html) is only a listening twin

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear a pattern they could build.
entries.content: A saved user pattern, Broken chord stabs, over a held chord.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 04-user-pattern (the lab/patterns/broken-chord-stabs.json pattern) (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear Time mode and a smooth Step time sweep.
entries.content: The Step time gliding from 250 ms to 25 ms and back with no transport needed: the arp accelerates into a buzz and slows down, with no gap or burst.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 10-time-mode (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear the three swing settings.
entries.content: Two bars each at straight (50.0 %), triplet feel (66.7 %) and the maximum (75.0 %).
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 05-swing (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear Velocity random, Gate random and the curve.
entries.content: Two bars each: plain, Velocity random 60, plus Gate random 60, then the curve at 100 (the bell); note starts never move.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 17-randomness (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear transposition steps in semitones and in scale degrees.
entries.content: Three steps of +12 semitones, then two steps of +2 scale degrees in C major, each dropping back to the start.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 06-transposition (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear Latch (Replace and Add) and the sustain pedal.
entries.content: Latch Replace (a second chord replaces the first), Latch Add (a pressed note is added, pressed again it is removed), then the sustain pedal down and up.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 15-latch-pedal (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear where the pattern begins under each Restart value.
entries.content: A three-three-two pattern over a chord pressed late in the bar with a beat click: New chord, Bar, Free.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 12-restart (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.content: Repeats 2: each chord arpeggiated twice then silence until the next chord; then Repeats at forever.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 11-repeats (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear Quantize in Scale and Chord root.
entries.content: A six-note cluster as played, snapped to A minor, then the movable shape following the lowest held note.

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear the chord stage under the arp.
entries.content: One note at a time becomes a chord (major third and fifth, then an octave added) that sounds steadily while the arp plays its notes.

entries.purpose: Let the reader hear Arp as a chord generator.
entries.content: Arp on off, Chord on: a short melody comes out as chords lasting as long as each key; major, then minor.
entries.source: tests/core/render.cpp scenario 09-chord-generator (rendered by bash tools/render_listening.sh from the shipped core; the files land in the gitignored build/listen/)
